oewn-02380222-v.learner: to do an activity or take part in one; to be involved in something.
examples: there I readily engaged in the office of pointing out to my friend the certain evils of such a choice

oewn-00601765-v.learner: to take up all of someone's attention or all of their time.
examples: Miss Bingley's attention was quite as much engaged in watching Mr. Darcy's progress through his book, as in reading her own

oewn-00888123-v.learner: to promise a person to someone else in marriage.
examples: Her father engaged her to a man she had never met.

oewn-07958392-n.learner: any set of human beings, men or women or children, thought of together as a group.
examples: Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room
there was not such a variety of people to be met with in the country as in town

oewn-08177175-n.learner: all the citizens of a country or a state, taken together.
examples: The people of that country chose a new ruler.

oewn-07987588-n.learner: the members of your family, taken through the generations.
examples: Her people had farmed the same land for a hundred years.

oewn-02584957-v.learner: to do what a rule, a promise, or an agreement says you should do.
examples: I assure you I was very much disappointed that you did not come back and keep your engagement

oewn-01187158-v.learner: to give someone the things they need to live, and to support them.
examples: He earns just enough to keep a wife and three children.

oewn-02687605-v.learner: to make someone or something stay in the same state, place, or activity.
examples: The noise from the street kept the baby awake all night.

oewn-05825971-n.learner: one single fact taken by itself, apart from the whole of the matter.
examples: there cannot be two opinions on that point
Mrs. Reynolds could interest her on no other point.

oewn-06619161-n.learner: the real meaning of something, put in a few words.
examples: She talked for half an hour before she came to the point.

oewn-08637636-n.learner: the exact spot where something is; a place with narrow limits.
examples: From that point on the hill you can see the whole valley.

oewn-06033377-n.learner: an average of some numbers, worked out by adding them up in a set way and then dividing by a number that depends on how many there are.
examples: The mean of 4, 8 and 9 is 7.

oewn-08577045-n.learner: the place where you are living at that time.
examples: if you were sure that they would not offer to send her home
when I returned home the ----shire was to leave Meryton in a week

oewn-03264208-n.learner: the building that someone lives in.
examples: They moved into a small home near the sea.

oewn-14537296-n.learner: a place around you where you are loved and feel safe.
examples: The children needed a warm home more than they needed money.

oewn-00817348-v.learner: to say something back to what someone has said or asked.
examples: She answered in the affirmative
She answered him in the usual way; and, after a moment's pause, added,--

oewn-00637941-v.learner: to give the right answer or the right solution to something.
examples: No one in the class could answer the riddle he set them.

oewn-00721514-v.learner: to do something in reply when a signal comes.
examples: A servant answered the door before she had finished knocking.

oewn-02971932-n.learner: a vehicle on wheels that is pulled by one horse or more.
examples: The carriage was sent to meet them at----, and they were to return in it by dinnertime.
Mrs. Long does not keep a carriage, and had to come to the ball in a hack chaise

oewn-05009987-n.learner: the way a person usually holds and moves their body.
examples: Her upright carriage made her look taller than she was.

oewn-03901563-n.learner: the part of a train that passengers ride in.
examples: We found two seats in the last carriage of the train.

oewn-01955339-v.learner: to make a person or a thing go somewhere.
examples: you may send them by themselves, which perhaps will be still better
they were all sent to one of the windows to admire the view

oewn-01033289-v.learner: to cause something to be carried or passed on to another place.
examples: you send me full powers to act in your name throughout the whole of this business

oewn-01439891-v.learner: to cause or order something to be taken or passed on to another place.
examples: The office sent out the notices the same afternoon.

oewn-05624029-n.learner: having the qualities, above all the qualities of mind, that are needed to do something or get it done.
examples: it was not in her power to give any information of so satisfactory a nature
Mary's powers were by no means fitted for such a display

oewn-05198072-n.learner: having influence strong enough to control someone or something.
examples: My youngest sister has left all her friends--has eloped; has thrown herself into the power of--of Mr. Wickham.

oewn-13968154-n.learner: the hold on office that a government or an official has while in charge.
examples: The party had been in power for almost ten years.
